1.
Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR in FIR No.449/2022 under Section 279/337/304A IPC registered at PS Jyoti Nagar.

Facts in brief are that on 25.06.2022 deceased Smt.Saroj was going to Surya Nagar from Ashok Nagar and at about 01.05 p.m. when she reached in front of Harnam Palace, towards Nand Nagri, suddenly offending vehicle/bike bearing registration no.DL-5SCU-2236 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules hit the deceased due to which she received grievous and fatal injuries.
Deceased was taken to GTB Hospital where post mortem was conducted on the body of deceased.

It is stated that respondent no.1/driver of the offending vehicle was juvenile at the time of accident, respondent no.2 is stated to be owner of the offending vehicle and it was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

2. It is stated that at the time of accident deceased was doing a private job as a private attendant and was earning about Rs.30,000/- per month apart from doing part time work of massage while earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
After completion of investigation by local police, DAR in this case was filed.
3. Upon filing of DAR, respondents appeared before the Tribunal.
Respondent no.1 has filed the reply to the DAR wherein an MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 2 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:06:33
+0530 objection has been taken that a false FIR has been registered; respondent no.1 has been falsely implicated by the petitioners in collusion with police.
It is pleaded that vehicle was insured with respondent no.3/insurance company under policy no.2312910168852300000 valid from 06.03.2022 to 05.03.2027.

It is pleaded that respondent no.1 is a minor boy aged about 16 years and is a student of 10 th class and his name has been falsely given by the eye witness, however respondent no.1 was neither present at the spot nor involved in the accident.

It is further pleaded that on 30.06.2022 at about 8.00 a.m. police officials of PS Jyoti Nagar visited the house of respondent no.1 and took him and his father to police station, got R1 medically examined and sent him home thereafter.
After about one week, police again called respondent no.1 and his father to police station, got them signed papers and falsely implicated R1 in the present false case.
Contents of DAR have been totally denied.
4. No reply to DAR has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2.

5. Reply to the DAR has also been filed by respondent no.3/insurance company wherein an objection has been taken that at the time of accident offending vehicle was being used in public place in violation of section 4, 18, 129, 177 and 181 of M.V. Act.
It is pleaded that driver of the vehicle is a minor and was charge sheeted by police u/s 279/337/304A IPC and u/s 4/181, 128/177 and 129/177 of M.V. Act.
It is stated that since driver and owner have violated the terms and conditions of insurance policy as driver was driving the insured vehicle without valid and effective DL.

It is further stated that three people were riding on the insured vehicle at the time of accident which Dar-Pritee vs Ccl Baljeet Singh @ Lucky on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49160438/
2 amounts to violation of policy terms and conditions as well as M.V. Act, therefore R3/insurance is not liable to pay compensation.

128, 134(C), 129, 149, 158, 158(6), 170, 172, 177, 181, 185 of M.V. Act, section 64VB of Insurance Act.
However it is admitted that vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3.
Contents of DAR have been denied.

6. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 27.10.2023 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle No.DL5SCU-2236 on 25.06.2022 at about 01.05 pm at Main Road, Ashok Nagar, Opposite Harman Palace,
towards Bhajanpura, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Jyoti Nagar in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Smt.Saroj?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
7. In order to substantiate their case petitioners have examined two witnesses.
PW1 is Ms.Pritee (daughter of deceased) and PW2 is Gaurav, son of deceased who is stated to be eye witness of the accident.
8. No evidence has been led on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2.
On behalf of respondent no.3, one witness R3W1 Ms.Shaima Khurseed, officer of insurance company has been examined.
9. I have heard Sh.Amit Sharma, ld. counsel for petitioner and Sh.S.P.S. Chauhan, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have gone through their submissions and entire material available on record.

Issue No.1 10. It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 4 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:06:49 +0530 principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: Petitioners have examined PW2 Gaurav who is son as well as eye witness of the accident.
PW2 deposed that he is eye witness of the present case and stated that on 25.06.2022 at about 1.00 pm he along with his deceased mother was going to Surya Nagar, Ghaziabad from his house.

PW2 stated that when he along with his mother reached Wazirabad Road and they were crossing the road,
suddenly three boys were coming on a motorcycle make Splendor of black colour bearing registration no.DL- 5SCU-2236 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the mother of PW2 namely Saroj Devi due to which his mother fell on the road and sustained grievous and fatal injuries.
Witness says that thereafter he took her mother to GTB Hospital where doctor declared her brought dead.
Witness says that said accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.

12. From the above testimony of eye witness PW2 it is apparent that he has given the account of accident and the manner in which it MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:06:56 +0530 occurred.

From the perusal of evidence of PW2 it is evident that witness has specifically testified that accident occurred when he along with his deceased mother was crossing the road and due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 while driving offending vehicle no. DL-5SCU- 2236.
PW2 was duly cross examined, however nothing came in his cross- cross-examination to disbelieve the testimony of witness regarding rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

Even otherwise evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from police case documents which are Ex.PW1/2 including copy of FIR, statement of PW2 Gaurav Singh, site plan, mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, reply to notice u/s 133 M.V. Act by the owner of the offending vehicle wherein owner/ respondent no.2 has stated that at the time of accident said motorcycle was being driven by respondent no.1, MLC, post mortem report of deceased etc.
Report u/s 173 Cr.P.C. by the local police is also part of DAR in which respondent no.1 has been prosecuted for committing accident in question.
13. Factum of negligence can well be stated by the fact that respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle was himself a minor and was not supposed to drive the vehicle.
Obviously respondent no.1 was not having any driving licence being a minor.
This fact in itself also shows that a minor driving the vehicle is impliedly taking imminent risk of driving without care and caution on account of being minor.
As such this Tribunal concludes that factum of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 has been proved by preponderance of probability by petitioners.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 14.

In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to MACT No.538/2022 Digitally signed Page 6 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:07:03 +0530 get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).

sentences.text: COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 15.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Smt.Saroj.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 8 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
16.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
17.
So far as age of the deceased is concerned, copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased Smt.Saroj is annexed with documents of DAR wherein date of birth of deceased is mentioned to be 20.03.1973.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased in the absence of any evidence contrary to the same.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (25.06.2022) was 49 years.
Assessment of Income of deceased :

18. Petitioner no.2/PW1 (daughter of deceased) in her deposition stated that her deceased mother was doing private job as private attendant and was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month and she was also doing part time work of massage in Delhi and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
During cross examination PW1 though stated that her mother was working in day and night as nursing, however she has not filed any diploma regarding nursing.

PW1 also admitted that she has Dar-Pritee vs Ccl Baljeet Singh @ Lucky on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49160438/

In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as nursing attendant or that she used to earn Rs.400,000/- per month at the time of her death.

In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.16,506/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:

As held above, deceased was 49 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

Future Prospects:

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

22. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 49 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (aged between 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
25.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Perusal of the said judgment would show that in para 13 Hon'ble Supreme Court in its wisdom awarded the rate of interest to be 6%, without any specific reasons mentioned in the judgment.

Awarding of interest obviously is within the discretion of the superior courts but in the absence of any legal proposition laid down, this Tribunal is of considered view that amount of interest on the compensation should be just and fair in the light of prevailing interest in banking transactions.
Therefore petitioners are entitled for interest @ 8% per annum from the date of institution till realization on the amount of compensation as computed above.

sentences.text: R3W1 says that insurance company is not liable either to indemnify any loss to insured nor liable to pay any compensation on account of breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy Ex.R3W1/2.

Witness says that a notice under Order 12 Rule 8 r/w section 151 CPC and u/s 134(c) of M.V. Act was sent to driver and owner of vehicle no.DL-5CU-2236 to produce copy of valid and effective DL of driver but they both failed to place the same on record.

Witness proved copy of notice along with postal receipts and tracking report as Ex.R3W1/3.
31.
In view of the evidence of PW R3W1 and the admitted fact by the respondent no.1 in its reply to the DAR that he was minor at the time of accident.

It has also come in the report filed by the local police under Section 173 Cr.PC that respondent no.1 has been prosecuted in the criminal case being minor driver of the offending vehicle without any valid driving licence.

Thus there is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy of offending vehicle as the same was being driven by a minor/respondent no.1 and that too without any valid and effective driving licence.

Therefore though insurance company is directed to pay amount of compensation to the petitioners however with liberty to recover the same from respondent no.2/owner of the offending vehicle as respondent no.1 was minor at the time of accident.
32. Having considered the facts, once this Tribunal has already concluded to give recovery rights to the insurance company, plea of ld.
Counsel for the insurance regarding giving directions to owner and driver for giving security of the amount of compensation.
It be noted that MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 15 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:08:01 +0530
judgment of Nanjappan case (supra) as relied upon does not lay down a ratio to be applied in every possible case.

In peculiar circumstances of that case the Hon'ble Apex Court while setting aside the order of Hon'ble High Court, considered it expedient in facts of that case for ensuring the due enforcement of recovery rights, by giving directions for security to be furnished by owner of the offending vehicle.

Question of giving such directions would be in parity with order of attachment before judgment as provided under Order 38 Rule 5 CPC, furnishing of security can be ordered only when there is evidence available on the record establishing that respondent/judgment debtor is about to dispose of all or any part of his property, or to flee away from the judicial process.
In the absence of any such situation existing in the present case, no such directions are warranted.

opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by this Tribunal on 27.10.2023 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle No.DL5SCU-2236 on 25.06.2022 at about 01.05 pm at Main Road, Ashok Nagar, Opposite Harman Palace,
towards Bhajanpura, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Jyoti Nagar in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Smt.Saroj?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
13. Factum of negligence can well be stated by the fact that respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle was himself a minor and was not supposed to drive the vehicle.
Obviously respondent no.1 was not having any driving licence being a minor.
This fact in itself also shows that a minor driving the vehicle is impliedly taking imminent risk of driving without care and caution on account of being minor.
As such this Tribunal concludes that factum of accident having occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 has been proved by preponderance of probability by petitioners.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased in the absence of any evidence contrary to the same.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (25.06.2022) was 49 years.
In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as nursing attendant or that she used to earn Rs.400,000/- per month at the time of her death.
In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in Delhi which at the time of accident was of Rs.16,506/- per month.
Application of Multiplier:
19.
As held above, deceased was 49 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para MACT No.538/2022 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 11 MALIK Date: 2024.07.15 16:07:35 +0530 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)
24.
Awarding of interest obviously is within the discretion of the superior courts but in the absence of any legal proposition laid down, this Tribunal is of considered view that amount of interest on the compensation should be just and fair in the light of prevailing interest in banking transactions.
Therefore petitioners are entitled for interest @ 8% per annum from the date of institution till realization on the amount of compensation as computed above.
In view of the evidence of PW R3W1 and the admitted fact by the respondent no.1 in its reply to the DAR that he was minor at the time of accident.
Thus there is fundamental breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy of offending vehicle as the same was being driven by a minor/respondent no.1 and that too without any valid and effective driving licence.
Therefore though insurance company is directed to pay amount of compensation to the petitioners however with liberty to recover the same from respondent no.2/owner of the offending vehicle as respondent no.1 was minor at the time of accident.
Question of giving such directions would be in parity with order of attachment before judgment as provided under Order 38 Rule 5 CPC, furnishing of security can be ordered only when there is evidence available on the record establishing that respondent/judgment debtor is about to dispose of all or any part of his property, or to flee away from the judicial process.
In the absence of any such situation existing in the present case, no such directions are warranted.
